note.question: How much project-quality information should be disclosed when a startup rolls over debt so that it can raise the most initial funding without sacrificing more social welfare than necessary?
note.overview: An entrepreneur, an informed inside creditor, and competing outside creditors play a three-date incomplete-information lending and refinancing game. Creditors make strategic startup and rollover offers, the insider conditions its response on privately observed project quality, outsiders update from a public signal, and the entrepreneur chooses costly effort. The paper explicitly uses perfect Bayesian equilibrium and jointly designs information disclosure and the short-term loan contract.

components.label: Solution or estimation method
components.explanation: The authors solve the three-date game by backward induction for a fixed signal structure and startup-loan contract, derive the insider's equilibrium returns with and without outside refinancing, and then compare monotone disclosure rules. Pooling all outsider-entry signals and all outsider-exclusion signals yields a binary structure; aligning its signal threshold with the entrepreneur's effort threshold gives V(p_T), which is optimized analytically. The same decomposition is used to solve the welfare problem and derive comparative statics.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Before financing, a regulator or third-party intermediary commits to a monotone public signal structure. At day 0, the entrepreneur needs B and creditors simultaneously offer startup loans; the lowest requested day-1 repayment wins and that creditor becomes the insider. At day 1, project quality p and independent creditor liquidity shocks are realized; the entrepreneur and insider observe p, whereas outsiders observe only signal s. Outsiders simultaneously make refinancing offers, and an unshocked insider then matches the lowest outside offer or exits, or sets its own offer when no outsider participates.

components.label: Perfect Bayesian equilibrium of the startup-loan and debt-rollover game
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Perfect Bayesian equilibrium of the startup-loan and debt-rollover game. Section 2.4 explicitly defines perfect Bayesian equilibrium E(B; sigma): creditors use behavioral loan-offer and refinancing strategies, the entrepreneur conditions effort on realized quality and accepted loans, and outsiders update beliefs by Bayes' rule. Under the optimal pass-or-fail structure, outsiders compete after a pass and offer v-c/p_T, inducing work exactly for p at or above p_T; after a fail they stay out, so an unshocked insider refinances as a monopolist and extracts the positive net surplus. Perfect day-0 competition equates the insider's expected return to B.
